metadata.schema: HRIS (6 tables: departments, employees, attendance_logs, payroll, projects, employee_projects)
metadata.notes: Expected SQL uses column names from the actual database schema. Some questions may have multiple valid SQL solutions.

questions.question: List all departments
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM departments

questions.question: Show all employees
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM employees

questions.question: What projects exist in the system?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM projects

questions.question: Show all employee job titles
questions.expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT job_title FROM employees

questions.question: List all attendance records
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM attendance_logs

questions.question: Show all payroll records
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM payroll

questions.question: List all project statuses
questions.expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT status FROM projects

questions.question: How many employees are in the system?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees

questions.question: How many departments are there?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM departments

questions.question: Show the names and emails of all employees
questions.expected_sql: SELECT name, email FROM employees

questions.question: Show employees hired after 2023
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE hire_date > '2023-12-31'

questions.question: Which employees have a salary greater than 8000?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE salary > 8000

questions.question: Show ongoing projects only
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM projects WHERE status = 'Ongoing'

questions.question: List employees who are Software Engineers
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE job_title = 'Software Engineer'

questions.question: Show attendance records where status is Absent
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM attendance_logs WHERE status = 'Absent'

questions.question: List completed projects
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM projects WHERE status = 'Completed'

questions.question: Show employees whose name starts with A
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE name LIKE 'A%'

questions.question: Which projects have a budget greater than 100000?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM projects WHERE budget > 100000
questions.description: Filter with numeric comparison on budget

questions.question: What is the average salary of all employees?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees

questions.question: What is the total budget of all projects?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT SUM(budget) FROM projects

questions.question: How many employees are in each department?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT department_id, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id

questions.question: What is the average salary per department?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT department_id, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id

questions.question: What is the highest salary in the company?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT MAX(salary) FROM employees

questions.question: What is the lowest salary in the company?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT MIN(salary) FROM employees

questions.question: How many projects have each status?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM projects GROUP BY status
questions.description: GROUP BY with COUNT on projects

questions.question: What is the total bonus amount paid across all payroll records?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT SUM(bonus) FROM payroll

questions.question: What is the average base salary in payroll?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT AVG(base_salary) FROM payroll

questions.question: How many attendance records are there for each status?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM attendance_logs GROUP BY status

questions.question: Show employee names with their department names
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, d.name FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id
questions.description: Basic JOIN between employees and departments

questions.question: List employees who work in the Engineering department
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.* FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id WHERE d.name = 'Engineering'

questions.question: Show employees and the projects they are working on
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, p.project_name, ep.role FROM employees e JOIN employee_projects ep ON e.id = ep.employee_id JOIN projects p ON ep.project_id = p.id

questions.question: List all employees with their payroll details
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, p.month_year, p.base_salary, p.bonus FROM employees e JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id

questions.question: Show attendance records with employee names
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, a.log_date, a.status FROM employees e JOIN attendance_logs a ON e.id = a.employee_id

questions.question: Which employees are working on the Website Redesign project?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, ep.role FROM employees e JOIN employee_projects ep ON e.id = ep.employee_id JOIN projects p ON ep.project_id = p.id WHERE p.project_name = 'Website Redesign'

questions.question: Show the total budget of projects each employee is involved in
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, SUM(p.budget) FROM employees e JOIN employee_projects ep ON e.id = ep.employee_id JOIN projects p ON ep.project_id = p.id GROUP BY e.id
questions.description: JOIN with GROUP BY and SUM

questions.question: List departments and how many employees each has
questions.expected_sql: SELECT d.name, COUNT(e.id) FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.id

questions.question: Show employees and their roles in projects
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, p.project_name, ep.role FROM employees e JOIN employee_projects ep ON e.id = ep.employee_id JOIN projects p ON ep.project_id = p.id

questions.question: What is the average salary by department name?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT d.name, AVG(e.salary) FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.id
questions.description: JOIN with GROUP BY and AVG

questions.question: Which employees work on more than one project?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, COUNT(ep.project_id) FROM employees e JOIN employee_projects ep ON e.id = ep.employee_id GROUP BY e.id HAVING COUNT(ep.project_id) > 1

questions.question: Which department has the highest average salary?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT d.name, AVG(e.salary) as avg_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.id ORDER BY avg_salary DESC LIMIT 1
questions.description: GROUP BY with ORDER BY and LIMIT

questions.question: List the top 3 highest paid employees
questions.expected_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 3

questions.question: Which employees have never been absent?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e WHERE e.id NOT IN (SELECT employee_id FROM attendance_logs WHERE status = 'Absent')

questions.question: What is the total payroll cost per department?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT d.name, SUM(p.base_salary + p.bonus) FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id JOIN payroll p ON e.id = p.employee_id GROUP BY d.id
questions.description: Multi-table JOIN with arithmetic and GROUP BY

questions.question: Which project has the most employees assigned to it?
questions.expected_sql: SELECT p.project_name, COUNT(ep.employee_id) as employee_count FROM projects p JOIN employee_projects ep ON p.id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.id ORDER BY employee_count DESC LIMIT 1
questions.description: JOIN with GROUP BY, ORDER BY, and LIMIT

questions.question: Show departments where the average salary is above 6000
questions.expected_sql: SELECT d.name, AVG(e.salary) as avg_salary FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.id HAVING AVG(e.salary) > 6000
questions.description: GROUP BY with HAVING on aggregate

questions.question: List employees who have both Present and Absent attendance records
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name FROM employees e JOIN attendance_logs a ON e.id = a.employee_id WHERE a.status IN ('Present', 'Absent') GROUP BY e.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.status) = 2

questions.question: Rank employees by salary within each department
questions.expected_sql: SELECT name, department_id, salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) as rank FROM employees

questions.question: Show the running total of payroll by month
questions.expected_sql: SELECT month_year, base_salary + bonus as total, SUM(base_salary + bonus) OVER (ORDER BY month_year) as running_total FROM payroll

questions.question: Find the highest paid employee in each department using a subquery
questions.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, e.salary, e.department_id FROM employees e WHERE e.salary = (SELECT MAX(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department_id = e.department_id)

questions.question: Show department budgets compared to their total employee salaries using a CTE
questions.expected_sql: WITH dept_salary AS (SELECT department_id, SUM(salary) as total_salary FROM employees GROUP BY department_id) SELECT d.name, d.budget, ds.total_salary FROM departments d JOIN dept_salary ds ON d.id = ds.department_id
